newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal parties open way to electoral reform.
newsitem.headline: Portugal parties open way to electoral reform.

text.p: Portugal's ruling Socialist Party and its main opposition agreed on Tuesday on proposals for constitutional changes that would open the way to electoral reform and allow referendums.

Prime Minister Antonio Guterres had promised a referendum on European Union plans to revise its Maastricht Treaty, the blueprint for economic and monetary union, and his proposals for a system of regional governments in Portugal.
Referendums are not permitted under Portugal's existing constitution.

The proposed reforms would also allow Portugal's near pure proportional representation system to be modified, including the eventual introduction of British-style constituencies, and cut the number of members of parliament from 230 at present.

Leaders of the Socialist and Social Democrat parties, which together hold 85 percent of the seats in parliament, were due to a present a final text for the proposed constitutional changes to their parliamentary parties later on Tuesday.

The accord, which was angrily attacked by the remaining two parties in parliament, the right-wing Popular Party and the Communists, will be officially signed by the Socialists and the Social Democrats on Sunday.
The Popular Party and the Communists object that reforms to something as fundamental as the constitution should have been the subject of all-party talks.
The two major parties also agreed to give the vote to Portuguese emigrants in presidential elections provided that they met certain conditions which have still to be spelled out.
